tokens.nirañjana: O stainless one, free from stain (voc.)
tokens.parātpara: O higher-than-the-highest / supreme beyond the supreme (voc.)

translations.close: O Nandīśa, O Lord of all beings, O stainless one, O supreme beyond the supreme!

tokens.nirañjanapadaṃ: the state (pada) of the Stainless One (acc.)

translations.close: By what means, O Lord of the gods, may one obtain the state of the Stainless One?

tokens.samayācāravidhānañca: and the rule of samaya-conduct (samayācāra-vidhāna + ca)
tokens.sādhanañca: and the sādhana (means of attainment; ca)

translations.close: Reveal the ordinance of samaya conduct and the sādhana.
I wish to hear all that — and (it is) for the welfare of sādhakas.
O Mahādeva, reveal to me the great Yoni, (bound by) the oath.

tokens.sāragamyañca: and the essence to be attained (sāra-gamya + ca)

translations.close: Reveal to me that essence — the essence attainable (from) the Vedas.

tokens.sārātsārataraṃ: more essential than the essential (sārāt + sārataram)

translations.close: O Goddess, (it is) more essential than the essential, higher than the supreme — the highest of all.
Truth, truth, again truth — truth, truth, truth, again and again.
But this supreme secret is hard to obtain in the three worlds.
It cannot be told even by a thousand (series of) other births.
It must be concealed, must be concealed, must be concealed — by you, again.
Whoever does not know the mantra's meaning, the mantra's consciousness, and the yoni-mudrā —

tokens.sūreśvari: O Sūreśvarī (voc.; goddess, 'Mistress of the Sun')

translations.close: I will tell the great mantra and the meaning-essence of the mantra, O Sūreśvarī.
And only by purity of mind, O beloved of Prāṇa, (is) the mantra's meaning (attained).
Kālī, Tārā, Mahādevī, Bhuvaneśī, and Ṣoḍaśī.
And Bagalā, Mātaṅgī, and Kamalā are proclaimed.

tokens.mokṣā: liberation (mokṣā; verse pattern suggests mokṣadā 'bestower of liberation')

translations.close: The Goddess is the bestower of enjoyment and liberation, concealed by ten million brahmāṇḍas (universes).

tokens.devadevaprā: life-breath of the God of gods (devadeva-prāṇa-) [fragment]
tokens.sarvadevasvarūpi: having the form of all gods (sarvadeva-svarūpiṇī) [fragment]

translations.close: She is made of the life-breath of the God of gods; she has the form of all gods.

tokens.sṛṣṭisthitikarī: she who effects creation and maintenance

translations.close: The Goddess who effects creation and maintenance, having the form of Viṣṇu, is Maheśvarī.
By the mere hearing of her, the sādhaka becomes liberated while living.
Having heard that, all the ancestors dance, their minds filled with joy.

tokens.adeyāpi: even though not to be given (adeyā + api)

translations.close: Even though it is not to be given, the Mahāvidyā bestows full fruit in the Kali age.

tokens.āgamoktavidhānena: by the rule declared in the Āgama (instr.)

translations.close: In the Kali age, the wise one should worship the gods by the rule declared in the Āgama.
Kālikā, O Goddess, bestows liberation in the Kali age — she grants swift fruit.
Brahmāṇī performs creation, but never Brahmā.
Protection (is done) by Vaiṣṇavī, O Goddess, but never by Viṣṇu.
Rudrāṇī performs the devouring, but never Rudra.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and the rest are proclaimed to be mere inert matter (jaḍa).
Because of whom the best of sādhakas performs dharma, adharma, and the like.

tokens.saṃpradāyavidhānena: by the rule of the tradition (saṃpradāya-vidhāna, instr.)

translations.close: And it must be done according to the rule of the tradition, O Maheśvarī.
She who is Kṛṣṇā — she indeed is Kṛṣṇa; likewise Brahmā is proclaimed.
But whoever, of deluded intellect, thinks (them) distinct — he is a sinner.

tokens.abhedañcintayedyastu: who indeed thinks non-distinction (abheda + cintayet + yaḥ + tu)

translations.close: But whoever thinks (them) non-distinct — he is a yogin; here there is no doubt.

tokens.vaṃśīnādavinodena: by the delight of the flute's sound (instr.)

translations.close: By the delight of the flute's sound, she deludes the entire world.
In the Kali age, having attained blackness, she is dark-blue in form even though she is white.

tokens.tārakatvāt: because of (her) ferrying-across / saving nature (tāraka-tva, abl.)

translations.close: Because of her saving (tāraka) nature, Tārā is always proclaimed 'Tāriṇī'.

tokens.sṛṣṭisthitikarī: she who effects creation and maintenance

translations.close: The Goddess who effects creation and maintenance is also called Bhuvaneśī.
And the Great Goddess, devoid of qualities, is proclaimed Ṣoḍaśī.
And she, the wife of Kālabhairava, is proclaimed Bhairavī.
And the Great Goddess, possessed of the three guṇas, is the Enchantress Mohinī, bestower of liberation — certainly.

tokens.caturvargapradāyinī: bestower of the four aims (dharma, artha, kāma, mokṣa)

translations.close: The Great Goddess, having the form of smoke, is the bestower of the four aims (caturvarga).
In the letter va (resides) the Goddess Vāruṇī; in the letter ga she is declared the bestower of siddhi.

tokens.madaśīlatvānmataṅgāsuranāśinī: from (her) nature of intoxication, the destroyer of the demon Mataṅga (mada-śīla-tvāt + mataṅgāsura-nāśinī)

translations.close: Mātaṅgī, by her nature of intoxication, is the destroyer of the demon Mataṅga.
And the Goddess Kamalā, dwelling in Vaikuṇṭha, is proclaimed.
These ten are the Mahāvidyās; and (she) is called the Siddhavidyā.
In the Kali age, by whatever manner, she bestows full fruit.
To a heretic, to a rogue, and indeed to one devoid of qualities, and indeed to a reviler —

tokens.prakāśyamidaṃ: this is to be revealed (prakāśya + idam)

translations.close: This must not be revealed, O blessed one — it is my fixed oath, always.

tokens.āsāñcaiva: and indeed of these (āsām + ca + eva)

translations.close: Of these there is no equal — none in the three worlds, certainly.

tokens.deveśi: O Devī, Mistress of the gods (voc.)

translations.close: By mere remembrance (of her), O Devī, one is released from the bondage of worldly existence.
And indeed from Nirguṇā were born the three bindus.

tokens.āsīdavindustato: there was the Bindu; from that (āsīt + avinduḥ + tataḥ)
tokens.śaktisamudbhavaḥ: the arising of Śakti (Goddess-power / mantric power)

translations.close: There was the Bindu; from it (arose) the Nāda; from the Nāda, the arising of Śakti.

tokens.nādāccaiva: and indeed from the Nāda (nādāt + ca + eva)

translations.close: And indeed from the Nāda arose the half-Bindu (ardha-bindu), O Maheśvarī.
The Goddess is without qualities and with qualities, having the form of Brahman, eternal.
The Goddess, whose form is consciousness, illumines all beings.
And she is to be known as quality-less, as having the form of Brahman, and as alone (kevalā).

tokens.caturvedaprabhāvinī: she who irradiates the four Vedas

translations.close: Four-qualitied, O Maheśānī, she irradiates the four Vedas.

tokens.sarvaviśvaprabhāvinī: she who irradiates the entire universe

translations.close: The Great Goddess, possessed of all qualities, irradiates the entire universe.

tokens.surasundari: O beautiful one of the gods (voc.)

translations.close: The mother of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the rest — O beautiful goddess.

tokens.ekākṣarasvarūpi: having the form of the single syllable (eka-akṣara-rūpiṇī) [fragment]

translations.close: The Great Goddess, of one quality, has the form of the single syllable.
But the Great Goddess, three-qualitied, is proclaimed three-syllabled (tryakṣarī).

tokens.navākṣaraprakāśinī: she who illumines the nine syllables

translations.close: Nine-qualitied, O Maheśānī, she illumines the nine syllables.

tokens.tridaśātmikā: of the nature of the thirty

translations.close: And indeed in the twelve and the thirteen, (she is) the Twelfth, of the nature of the thirty.
The Goddess, of the nature of fifteen, illumines the fifteen.

tokens.daśasaptaga: the group of ten and seven (daśa-sapta-gaṇa-) [fragment]

translations.close: Endowed with the group of ten and seven, she is proclaimed the Seventeen.
Endowed with twenty-eight, she has a form supremely worthy of worship.
The mantras with more than twenty syllables are proclaimed the garland-mantras.
She is proclaimed twenty-three, twenty-four, (and) twenty-five.
Endowed with twenty-eight, she is proclaimed (as) twenty-eight.

tokens.triṃśadādyāścatuḥṣaṣṭi: thirty and the rest up to sixty-four (triṃśat + ādyāḥ + catuḥṣaṣṭi)

translations.close: Beginning with thirty up to sixty-four, they are proclaimed the long mantras.

tokens.śaktimantrāśca: and the Śakti-mantras (mantras of the Goddess-power)

translations.close: Those mantras that are joined with svāhā are the Śakti-mantras, O Pārvatī.

tokens.pārvatīparameśvarasaṃvāde: in the dialogue of Pārvatī and Parameśvara (loc.)

translations.close: Thus, in the Kubjikā Tantra, in the dialogue between Pārvatī and Parameśvara, (ends) the first chapter.
Without whom japa, worship, and the like would never be accomplished anywhere.
The letter ka is declared the bestower of desires; the letter ra is the destroyer of sin.
The Great Goddess has the form of Nāda, is devoid of qualities, (and) has the form of Brahman.

tokens.brahmarūpomakāraśca: and the letter Om having the form of Brahman (brahma-rūpa + omakāra + ca)

translations.close: And the letter Om, having the form of Brahman — it is both with qualities and without qualities.

tokens.caturvargaphalapradaḥ: bestower of the fruit of the four aims

translations.close: And the letter ī, having the form of Durgā, bestows the fruit of the four aims.
The letter ka is declared (to be) Varuṇa, the maker of the life-breath of the world.

tokens.bhavasaṃsāratāri: ferrying across the cycle of worldly existence (bhava-saṃsāra-tāriṇī) [fragment]

translations.close: In the letter ī (resides) the Goddess Tāriṇī, who ferries (beings) across the cycle of worldly existence.

tokens.vahnirūpoyaṃ: this one having the form of fire (vahni-rūpaḥ + ayam)

translations.close: The letter ra, having the form of fire, is the burner of the suffering of existence.
And when the Goddess is with qualities, she is the bestower of all siddhis.
The God is the bestower of nirvāṇa-liberation, the bestower of all siddhis.
In the letter u (resides) the Goddess Bhairavī, destroyer of all dangers.
And in the letter ha (is) the great Viṣṇu, destroyer of great sins.
In the letter u (resides) the Goddess Mohinī, who enchants the world.

tokens.syādukāre: should be; in the letter u (syāt + ukāre)

translations.close: The letter ha is Sadāśiva; and indeed in the letter u (is) Brahman.
By the mere remembrance of this, one would obtain (the fruit of) ten thousand Aśvamedha sacrifices.
In the letter ī (resides) the supreme Goddess, always consisting of the three guṇas.
The letter kṣa, the bestower of the field (kṣetra), is Viṣṇu, the destroyer of great sins.
And in the letter la (resides) the Goddess Caṇḍikā, destroyer of the demon Caṇḍa.

tokens.saśailavanakānanā: together with mountains, forests, and groves

translations.close: In the letter ka the earth is declared, together with its mountains, forests, and groves.

tokens.pṛthvīdānaphalapradā: bestower of the fruit of the gift of land

translations.close: In the letter la (is) the earth, O Goddess — the bestower of the fruit of the gift of land.
In the letter ka (is) Sundarī, O Goddess; in the letter e, she who has the form of the yoni.

tokens.paramātmakalā: the kalā (emanation-phase) of the Supreme Self

translations.close: And Parā, and indeed the highest Paramā — again, the kalā of the Supreme Self.
And in the letter ka (is) Mahādeva; and the letter ra, indeed, is Brahmāṇī.
The letter ī, bestower of desires, the beloved, is adorned with Nāda and Bindu.
The letter u (is) the Goddess Ṣoḍaśī; the letter ū (is) Bhuvaneśvarī.
The letter ha is Yoganidrā; and the letter ha is the supreme Lord.

tokens.rephaścaiva: and indeed the letter ra (repha + ca + eva)

translations.close: And indeed the letter ra, O Great Goddess, is adorned with Nāda and Bindu.
The single-syllabled one is the great Vidyā, the eternal knowledge of Brahman.
